evidence.summary: 让多个编程Agent共享Markdown记忆，通过DSH七个查询工具提供canonical路由、分层全文召回、弱匹配拒答和来源收据。
limitations: 功能摘要根据作者固定版本材料归纳，不是逐字引文或独立效果验证。

evidence.summary:
核查 README.md、package.json、extras/dsh/README.md、extras/dsh/lib/index.js、extras/dsh/lib/register.js、extras/dsh/lib/route.js、skill/krouter-obsidian/scripts/canonical_lookup.py、skill/krouter-obsidian/scripts/route_knowledge.py、skill/krouter-obsidian/scripts/recall_index.py、skill/krouter-obsidian/scripts/llm.py、skill/krouter-obsidian/scripts/krouter_redact.py、extras/host-daily-evolution/run.sh、extras/host-daily-evolution/resolve.py、SECURITY.md、docs/BENCHMARK.md；工具参数为短query，固定白名单只允许status/preference/correction/memory/project/search/suggest。runRoute按config/env选择vault与router，Windows优先Python，其它平台先shell，spawnSync带20秒timeout直接继承环境运行；没有调用ctx.subprocess或每会话vault选择。返回解析stdout首个同名冒号字段，模型文本输出仍需结合结构化ok/code与来源。

Python先查canonical alias映射和来源是否live，再输出来源/映射SHA-256与时间收据。exact并非只有逐字相等，规范化删除空格/标点，alias包含/被包含达到分数带也可锁源；同义语义仍依映射/词面。未锁定时FTS5按CJK双字/拉丁词召回，状态/tier提权，按分数底线、实词覆盖、库外词和margin决定confidence；缺乏足够覆盖报none，可扩到vault并显式标scope_widened，最后退字面检索。

贡献在把有效状态/旧页权重、纠错优先、弱匹配拒绝和可核对收据设为默认，并跨Agent共用透明库；作者自己说明匹配规则相同的BM25基线不显著落后。称“read-only”应限定为DSH不暴露写vault/别名工具，查询会刷新本地SQLite缓存并记查询JSONL，不能理解成机器上零写入。
limitations: 固定DSH注册/同步路由、Python canonical与FTS刷新/门控、状态/脱敏、writer lane opt-in与argv、nightly编排及作者benchmark方法；未完整审计shell/Python等价、备份加密或所有导入器，不运行目标。目录membership本轮unknown。
只执行本工程的统计和结构验证；没有执行目标插件、测试、安装或真实宿主验收。
GitHub/npm 活跃度只作采集背景，未核实独立用户采用或同条件收益对照。

findings.text:
面向跨Claude Code/Codex/Cursor/DSH工作的个人开发者，希望同一份Markdown记住决定与更改，不用每次重复说明。DSH包只提供七个查询工具接头，完整产品还含可选导入、夜间整理和备份，不会因dsh plugin add自动启动计时器。Obsidian是可选编辑/查看器，不是运行必须的服务。

合格查询是引用当前有效来源，旧决定被替代时先给纠错页，库里没有足够资料时明确不知道；最终Agent还需根据来源正确执行任务。canonical_match表示路由映射命中，不证明资料事实或模型答案正确，拒答率也需和可回答覆盖率一起看。

参照是grep/SQLite全文检索加手工笔记。插件在canonical有效页路由、ranked旧页降权、拒绝弱近邻和收据上有具体组合价值，不是新的语义向量检索。适合愿意维护可读笔记和明确适用范围的单用户；多人租户隔离、任意账户机密和无人审阅自进化不能只靠“第二大脑”文案保证。README的旧名DSH-KRouter可解释迁移线索，本轮目录成员关系仍unknown，不认定移除或确认当前收录。

工具参数为短query，固定白名单只允许status/preference/correction/memory/project/search/suggest。runRoute按config/env选择vault与router，Windows优先Python，其它平台先shell，spawnSync带20秒timeout直接继承环境运行；没有调用ctx.subprocess或每会话vault选择。返回解析stdout首个同名冒号字段，模型文本输出仍需结合结构化ok/code与来源。

Python先查canonical alias映射和来源是否live，再输出来源/映射SHA-256与时间收据。exact并非只有逐字相等，规范化删除空格/标点，alias包含/被包含达到分数带也可锁源；同义语义仍依映射/词面。未锁定时FTS5按CJK双字/拉丁词召回，状态/tier提权，按分数底线、实词覆盖、库外词和margin决定confidence；缺乏足够覆盖报none，可扩到vault并显式标scope_widened，最后退字面检索。

贡献在把有效状态/旧页权重、纠错优先、弱匹配拒绝和可核对收据设为默认，并跨Agent共用透明库；作者自己说明匹配规则相同的BM25基线不显著落后。称“read-only”应限定为DSH不暴露写vault/别名工具，查询会刷新本地SQLite缓存并记查询JSONL，不能理解成机器上零写入。
固定DSH注册/同步路由、Python canonical与FTS刷新/门控、状态/脱敏、writer lane opt-in与argv、nightly编排及作者benchmark方法；未完整审计shell/Python等价、备份加密或所有导入器，不运行目标。目录membership本轮unknown。
dsh-krouter v1.2.1 MIT，Node最低版本未声明，DSH三个通配peer；Python3/FTS5与可信vault/router为实际条件，DSH接头不安装timer。

#### 成本

| 阶段 | 现金与资源成本 | 人工与时间投入 | 已知条件与未知项 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 首次使用 | 路由/SQLite索引、个人Markdown材料 | 填有效决定与纠错状态，核库路径 | 作者110ms等不是本轮测量 |
| 持续使用 | 本地扫描/FTS刷新、每次同步spawn、查询日志 | 维护当前事实、审核引用与alias | 无向量服务，不代表零维护 |
| 可选写手 | 模型token、CLI进程、导入与备份 | 选择授权范围、检查nightly报告 | 每lane/库规模不同，无本轮费用/RSS |
| 失败恢复 | 原文/历史、查询收据与重建cache | 查误拒/错误引用、过期状态、写手变更 | 收据hash可核版本，不等于自动回滚 |
有条件试用lookup-only。先非敏感个人vault核对来源、旧页与拒答，保持原件；nightly/导入/writer按各lane权限另评，不把接头卸载当timer停止。详见[Q07](#research-q07)。

#### 效果

| 效果项 | 当前证据支持 | 尚不能确定 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 来源 | exact/recall收据、状态和SHA | 来源内容真实/当前任务适用 |
| 拒答 | 词面/coverage/库外词门槛 | 真用户错误引用与漏答平衡 |
| 纠错 | live页/替代状态参与路由 | 写手总能正确识别更改 |
| 跨Agent | 一个vault配多个socket | 多人隔离/所有客户端实际兼容 |

lookup本身没有模型调用，日志/缓存仍写本地；结果随后作为工具输出进入用户选定模型。作者held-out和真实开发集各有边界，匹配规则相同基线不显著落后。应把维护事实、拒答后人工查证、可选nightly消费与备份都计入，而非只算一次检索延迟。

夜间run.sh先执行writer，再按配置nightly步骤，dry-run走offline状态和各步发送量估计。DSH工具与nightly分开，插件卸载不自动删除vault，也不能据此认为外部系统timer已停止。导入、写手和备份要按实际安装路径判断，不能从包里存在代码推断用户已经授权或启用。

llm gate将Codex视可读整个账户的lane，只有点名或KROUTER_ALLOW_CODEX允许；其它不能约束CLI需ALLOW_UNCONFINED。writer_invoke为grok配置沙箱、Claude设dontAsk和带vault路径的工具白名单，Codex workspace-write+cwd vault。API文本lane不启本地Agent，但仍会把选定文本发模型。这里是程序参数/门控检查，不是本轮对第三方CLI强制约束的验收。

脱敏过滤已知key形态、label、URL/连接口令和secret页，不能覆盖任意无标识秘密或Agent自主读取。README/SECURITY也明确文本过滤不能管CLI自身读取；vault含不可信网页/聊天时，工具白名单与kernel沙箱不是同一种强度。备份/封账/修订链可提高恢复可读性，但对整个夜间写手和备份加密未做完整审计，不把作者“自动零维护”当无需审核。
将canonical有效状态、ranked分层权重、弱近邻拒绝与来源hash设为默认，跨Agent共用可编辑Markdown；相同两规则BM25基线并未被证明显著超越。详见[Q02](#research-q02)、[Q03](#research-q03)。
canonical过滤无效页，但ranked对旧页仅乘0.25仍可召回；metadata缓存与followlinks不构成新鲜度/物理沙箱。DSH同步执行和可选writer lane权限需分开，未做越界复现。详见[Q03](#research-q03)、[Q04](#research-q04)。
可探索来源版本/适用域/证据级别与冲突收据，区分词面lock和人工确认，比较跨项目错引、覆盖与维护开销；未实现。详见[Q07](#research-q07)。

technical.rationale: novelty为默认拒答/纠错状态/收据组合的实质增量；mechanism在词面lock与ranked门控有实质设计，非新检索模型；transferability为引用状态和弱近邻拒绝的显著可迁移启发；simplification为透明库/无向量服务的实质部署简化，但事实维护存在，不计未来适用域。

business.rationale: workflow让决定跨Agent复用有实质流程变化；delivery通过纠错引用/拒答辅助任务有实质能力，真实质量未知；reach为多Agent共一vault显著接入组合；economics仅减少重复说明潜力，未测人工与writer总成本。

recommendation.reason: lookup-only的共享笔记、拒答和来源收据值得非敏感单用户试用；审核当前状态与ranked旧页，nightly/导入/CLI另评，不能把canonical当事实认证。

scenario.rationale: 跨Agent重复决定与纠错场景明确，真实收益未测。

advantage.rationale: 拒答/状态/收据默认组合有实质差异。

evidence.rationale: 固定源码与作者方法核查，源码级50%档，实验未复跑。

cost.rationale: 本地lookup轻量，但库状态/alias和可选writer治理仍有负担。

publication.summaries.text: 让多个编程Agent共享Markdown记忆，通过DSH七个查询工具提供canonical路由、分层全文召回、弱匹配拒答和来源收据。

publication.capabilities.table:
| 能力 | 主要用途 | 使用条件与边界 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DSH接头 | 七查询工具调用本机router | 同步spawn、实例固定vault，非宿主沙箱 |
| canonical | alias锁定有效来源 | 词面启发，不是事实认证 |
| ranked recall | 本地FTS5与拒答门 | 旧页dead仅降权，可能误引/漏答 |
| 收据 | 来源/map SHA与状态/时间 | 可追版本，不自动确认内容适用 |
| 可选完整产品 | 导入/夜间写手/备份 | 不由DSH plugin add自动启用，另审权限 |

publication.advice.text: 有条件试用lookup-only。先非敏感个人vault核对来源、旧页与拒答，保持原件；nightly/导入/writer按各lane权限另评，不把接头卸载当timer停止。详见[Q07](#research-q07)。

      "path": "README.md",
      "content": "# KRouter\n\n**Your coding agents remember what you decided — and what you changed your mind about.**\n\nClaude Code, Codex, Cursor and DeepSeek Harness share one memory: a folder of plain Markdown in [Obsidian](https://obsidian.md) that you can read and edit. Ask \"how did we decide to ship?\" and the agent answers with the page it came from. A correction replaces the old answer instead of competing with it. When the vault does not know, the agent is told so, rather than handed something close.\n\n[![ci](https://github.com/398894496-arch/KRouter/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/398894496-arch/KRouter/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/398894496-arch/KRouter)](https://github.com/398894496-arch/KRouter/releases/latest) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) · 中文：[`README.zh.md`](README.zh.md)\n\n![Monday we decide A, Wednesday we change it to B, Thursday the agent answers B and cites the correction; a question the vault cannot answer is refused](docs/img/demo.gif)\n\n**Measured, not claimed.** On 200 held-out questions in English and Chinese that it was never tuned on, at default\nsettings, KRouter cites a wrong page 26% of the time; claude-mem 64%, basic-memory 78%. Of 80 questions the vault\ncannot answer, KRouter refuses 47; the other two refuse none. Of 60 questions about a decision that was later\nchanged, it gets 50 right; they get 34 and 16. Neither of them can refuse or knows a page was replaced, so part of\nthat gap is by construction: plain full-text search given KRouter's two rules is level with it. What KRouter adds is\nhaving those rules on by default, plus receipts and a vault you can edit. [How it was measured](docs/BENCHMARK.md#third-bench-200-held-out-questions-on-a-vault-nobody-tunes-on-2026-10-13) · [rerun it in one second](#check-it-yourself)\n\n## Install\n\n```bash\ncurl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/398894496-arch/KRouter/main/scripts/bootstrap.sh | sh\n```\n\nWindows (PowerShell): `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/398894496-arch/KRouter/main/scripts/bootstrap.ps1 | iex` · Claude Code plugin: `/plugin install krouter --marketplace 398894496-arch/KRouter` (Claude Code 2.1.275 or later; from a shell, `claude plugin install krouter --marketplace 398894496-arch/KRouter` needs 2.1.292). Third-party marketplaces do not auto-update: run `claude plugin update krouter@krouter`, or turn it on in `/plugin` → Marketplaces → krouter → Enable auto-update.\n\nRather look first? Nothing below changes your machine until the last line:\n\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/398894496-arch/KRouter.git && cd KRouter\n./scripts/first_run.sh                      # a receipt on the bundled sample vault\npython3 scripts/bootstrap.py --dry-run      # every change the install would make, made nowhere\npython3 scripts/bootstrap.py --vault ~/notes --no-timer   # install against your vault, nightly job off\n```\n\nPython 3 is the only requirement. The installer makes a vault (or uses yours with `--vault`, overwriting nothing), connects Claude Code and Codex to it through MCP, and stops there: lookup only, no questions, nothing leaves the machine. When you want it to start remembering, run the line it prints last (`bootstrap.py --ask`), which asks two questions.\n\n## Five minutes later\n\n1. Ask your agent: *\"what did we decide about X last week?\"* It answers from the vault, names the page, and says plainly when the vault has nothing on it.\n2. **\"Import the agent sessions already on this machine?\"** (with `--ask`) On a yes, the last 7 days of Claude Code, Codex and Cursor agent sessions become pages, one per session: your questions and each turn's closing answer. Key-shaped text is redacted first, and nothing leaves the machine.\n3. **\"Have your model pull out what was decided?\"** On a yes, the model you already use (a logged-in CLI or an API key) writes \"what was decided, what changed\" at the top of each recent session's page. The installer tells you how many characters that sends before it sends anything.\n\nFrom then on a nightly job, which also asks first, imports yesterday, distills it, and keeps the vault tidy. Nothing needs maintaining.\n\n## Is it for you?\n\n**Yes**, if you use Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or DeepSeek Harness (often more than one), keep notes in Markdown or\nwould, and keep re-explaining the same decision to your agents. **No**, if you want semantic search over\nembeddings, the last chat replayed into the next one, a hosted memory API, or a brain that is full on install.\n\n**Not only for code:** the same story for short-video work, recorded the same way (Claude Code with the plugin, a\ndemo vault, real output):\n\n![Monday the cover-title rule is A, Wednesday it changes to B, Thursday the agent answers B and cites the page; a question the vault has no page on is refused](docs/img/demo-content.gif)\n\n**Not needed:** Obsidian (it is an optional viewer), an alias table to maintain, an environment variable to set.\nAlready have a vault? `--vault` changes none of its files. The default is lookup only: no nightly job, no session\nimport.\n\n## How it is different\n\n| | KRouter | Typical agent memory |\n|---|---|---|\n| Where memory lives | Markdown pages you can open, edit, diff and sync | A database or vector store |\n| After a correction | The new page replaces the old one, which is marked superseded | Old and new chunks both match; you hope the right one wins |\n| When nothing matches | `recall: none` — the agent says the vault does not know | The nearest chunk, presented with confidence |\n| Every answer | Carries its source page and a receipt | Usually unsourced |\n| Who shares it | One vault for every agent on the machine (MCP, skill, rules) | Usually one tool |\n\n**Coming from [claude-mem](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem)?** Keep it. The importer has been run end to end against a live claude-mem 13.35.0 install. The installer finds its memory and offers to import it: session summaries become pages, and each project's decisions become one page you confirm. Your model can then sort those decisions into the ones still in force and the ones a later decision replaced, which claude-mem itself does not do. The Claude Code plugin also does what makes claude-mem feel like memory, in plain Markdown: when a session ends it is recorded, and when a new one starts, this repository's confirmed decisions and recent corrections come with it, each naming its page. Repositories are told apart by their path, never by folder name. Both happen only after you said yes to importing.\n\n## What leaves your machine\n\nQueries never do: lookup is a local SQLite full-text index, about 110 ms. Session import is local. Text goes to a model only for the steps you said yes to: distilling sessions and nightly upkeep. It goes to the CLI or API key you already use, and `--dry-run` shows the size first. Keys and pages marked secret are never sent or quoted. For the nightly writer, the API-key lane runs nothing on\nyour machine; CLI lanes differ in what they can read, and the install says which one you are choosing. Details:\n[`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md).\n\n**Backups.** `backup.py init --dir <a folder that syncs elsewhere>` turns on a nightly encrypted archive of the whole\nvault, history included, opened again each night before it counts. Point it at iCloud Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, a\nNetdisk sync folder or a USB disk (or two of them); KRouter talks to no cloud. Why this and not syncing or pushing the\nvault: [`DETAILS.md` → Backing up your vault](docs/DETAILS.md#backing-up-your-vault).\n\n## Honest numbers\n\n| Measured | Result |\n|---|---|\n| Refuses instead of guessing (public benches, CI) | Off-topic questions refused 12/12 (English) and 6/6 (Chinese) |\n| Wrong citations on a vault nobody tuned on ([third bench](docs/BENCHMARK.md#third-bench-200-held-out-questions-on-a-vault-nobody-tunes-on-2026-10-13), 200 held-out questions, English and Chinese, with daily-log distractors; 95% intervals) | At its default: KRouter 26% [19, 33] wrong, 47 / 80 neighbour questions refused, 102 / 120 answerable right; plain full-text search 58% [52, 65]. **Against a careful baseline it is level, not ahead:** plain search with the same two rules (leave replaced pages out, refuse below a floor) at the same coverage cites 42 wrong pages to KRouter's 36 and gets 96 right to 102, but neither difference is significant (paired intervals: wrong rate [-10.2, +1.3] points, right [-2, +14]). On the same 200 questions at their defaults, claude-mem 13.39 cites a wrong page 64% of the time [58, 71] and basic-memory 0.23 78% [72, 84]; neither refuses any of the 80 neighbour questions; of 60 questions about a changed decision they get 34 and 16 right, KRouter 50 |\n| Exact match vs embeddings on a supersede / neighbor set (CI) | Exact match refuses where TF-IDF, MiniLM and BGE-M3 cite a neighbor |\n| Real traffic, author's vault | 0.62 → 1.47 of 2, blind-judged. **This is a development set**: on held-out questions the gain is flat. A blind test on fresh traffic runs once 50 new queries are logged (not before 2026-10-20) |\n\n### Check it yourself\n\nNo install, no model, Python 3 only; the questions are in the repository and the numbers above come out in about a\nsecond:\n\n```bash\npython3 bench/memory_honesty/run.py --set heldout3 --ci                        # KRouter, with 95% intervals\npython3 bench/memory_honesty/run.py --set heldout3 --vs-matched bm25-floor    # against BM25 + the same two rules\n```\n\nMethods and what still fails: [`docs/VERIFY.md`](docs/VERIFY.md). For agents asked whether to recommend it:\n[`docs/FOR-AGENTS.md`](docs/FOR-AGENTS.md).\n\n## More\n\n- [How it works, every option](docs/DETAILS.md): install flags, the nightly writer, exact match and ranked recall, answer cards, the four agent mounts\n- [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md): what each model lane can see and do\n- [`docs/FOR-AGENTS.md`](docs/FOR-AGENTS.md): facts for an agent deciding whether KRouter fits its user\n- [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md) · [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md): good first issues are labeled\n\n*Formerly DSH-KRouter. Old links, clone URLs and install lines still redirect.* MIT.\n"

      "content": "import { existsSync, readFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\nimport { homedir } from \"node:os\";\nimport { join } from \"node:path\";\nimport { defineTool } from \"@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools\";\nimport z from \"@deepseek-ai/schemastery\";\nimport { registerKrouterTools } from \"./register.js\";\n\nexport const name = \"dsh-krouter\";\nexport const inject = [\"tools\"];\n\nfunction usable(val) {\n  const v = String(val || \"\").trim();\n  if (!v) return false;\n  return !/^(YOUR_|CHANGE_ME|REPLACE|TODO)/.test(v);\n}\n\nfunction isKeyName(name) {\n  return /(_API_KEY|_API_TOKEN)$/.test(name) || name === \"HF_TOKEN\" || name === \"KROUTER_CLI_LOGIN\";\n}\n\nfunction keyPresent() {\n  if (process.env.KROUTER_WRITER && existsSync(process.env.KROUTER_WRITER)) return true;\n  if (Object.keys(process.env).some((n) => isKeyName(n) && usable(process.env[n]))) return true;\n  const path = process.env.KROUTER_KEYS_ENV || join(homedir(), \".dsh-krouter-keys.env\");\n  if (existsSync(path)) {\n    for (const raw of readFileSync(path, \"utf8\").split(\"\\n\")) {\n      let line = raw.trim();\n      if (!line || line.startsWith(\"#\")) continue;\n      if (line.startsWith(\"export \")) line = line.slice(7);\n      const idx = line.indexOf(\"=\");\n      if (idx < 1) continue;\n      const name = line.slice(0, idx).trim();\n      const val = line.slice(idx + 1).trim().replace(/^[\"']|[\"']$/g, \"\");\n      if (isKeyName(name) && usable(val)) return true;\n    }\n  }\n  const vault = process.env.OBSIDIAN_VAULT || \"\";\n  const page = join(vault, \"90 系统文件\", \"自动化\", \"自进化钥匙.md\");\n  if (vault && existsSync(page)) {\n    for (const raw of readFileSync(page, \"utf8\").split(\"\\n\")) {\n      const m = raw.match(/^([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+)=(.*)$/);\n      if (m && isKeyName(m[1]) && usable(m[2])) return true;\n    }\n  }\n  return false;\n}\n\nexport const Config = z.object({\n  vaultPath: z\n    .string()\n    .default(\"\")\n    .description(\"Absolute Obsidian vault path. Empty uses OBSIDIAN_VAULT.\"),\n  routerScript: z\n    .string()\n    .default(\"\")\n    .description(\n      \"Absolute path to route_knowledge.sh. Empty uses KROUTER_ROUTER, then ~/.agents/skills/krouter-obsidian.\",\n    ),\n});\n\nexport function apply(ctx, config = {}) {\n  registerKrouterTools(ctx, config, defineTool);\n  if (!keyPresent()) {\n    console.error(\n      \"KRouter HOST ACTION: login a Claudian-class CLI (grok / official Codex / claude) or put *_API_KEY on the vault page / ~/.dsh-krouter-keys.env. [explicit, process.env.KROUTER_ROUTER, bundledPy, installedPy, bundled, installed]\n      : [explicit, process.env.KROUTER_ROUTER, bundled, installed, bundledPy, installedPy]\n  ).filter(Boolean);\n  for (const path of candidates) {\n    if (isForeignLiveRouter(path)) continue;\n    if (existsSync(path)) return path;\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nfunction pythonArgv(script, args) {\n  const exe = process.env.PYTHON || process.env.KROUTER_PYTHON || \"\";\n  if (exe) return [exe, [script, ...args]];\n  if (platform() === \"win32\") return [\"py\", [\"-3\", script, ...args]];\n  return [\"python3\", [script, ...args]];\n}\n\nexport function resolveVault(explicit) {\n  return explicit || process.env.OBSIDIAN_VAULT || process.env.KROUTER_VAULT || \"\";\n}\n\nexport function runRoute({ route, query = \"\", vault, router, timeoutMs = 20000 } = {}) {\n  if (!ALLOWED.has(route)) {\n    return {\n      ok: false,\n      code: 2,\n      stdout: \"\",\n      stderr: `refused route: ${route}. read-only: ${[...ALLOWED].join(\"|\")}\\n`,\n    };\n  }\n  const vaultRoot = resolveVault(vault);\n  if (!vaultRoot) {\n    return { ok: false, code: 2, stdout: \"\", stderr: \"set OBSIDIAN_VAULT or vaultPath\\n\" };\n  }\n  const script = resolveRouter(router);\n  if (!script) {\n    return {\n      ok: false,\n      code: 2,\n      stdout: \"\",\n      stderr: \"route_knowledge.sh not found. run ./scripts/install.sh or set KROUTER_ROUTER\\n\",\n    };\n  }\n  const args = [route];\n  if (query) args.push(query);\n  const isPy = String(script).endsWith(\".py\");\n  const result = isPy\n    ? spawnSync(...pythonArgv(script, args), {\n        encoding: \"utf8\",\n        timeout: timeoutMs,\n        cwd: dirname(script),\n        env: { ...process.env, OBSIDIAN_VAULT: vaultRoot },\n      })\n    : spawnSync(script, args, {\n        encoding: \"utf8\",\n        timeout: timeoutMs,\n        env: { ...process.env, OBSIDIAN_VAULT: vaultRoot },\n      });\n  return {\n    ok: result.status === 0,\n    code: result.status ??       "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Pick one canonical row for a literal query. Exit 1 if none or ambiguous.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport unicodedata\nfrom datetime import date\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\n# 别名表是宿主的资产，放在库里（跟着库同步、进库的 git 快照），代码目录里那份只是样例兜底。\nMAP_REL = \"90 系统文件/canonical_sources.psv\"\n\n\ndef map_for(vault: Path | None) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"The alias table in force: `KROUTER_MAP`, else the vault's own table, else the shipped sample.\"\"\"\n    raw = os.environ.get(\"KROUTER_MAP\", \"\").strip()\n    if raw:\n        return Path(raw)\n    if vault is not None:\n        sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))\n        import zones\n\n        if zones.path(vault, MAP_REL).is_file():\n            return zones.path(vault, MAP_REL)\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent / \"canonical_sources.psv\"\n\n\nPARTICLES = set(\"的了着过地得\")\n\n\ndef parse_frontmatter(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:\n    if not path.is_file():\n        return {}\n    text = path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n    if not text.startswith(\"---\"):\n        return {}\n    parts = text.split(\"---\", 2)\n    if len(parts) < 3:\n        return {}\n    found: dict[str, str] = {}\n    for raw in parts[1].splitlines():\n        line = raw.strip()\n        if not line or line.startswith(\"#\") or \":\" not in line:\n            continue\n        name, val = line.split(\":\", 1)\n        found[name.strip()] = val.strip().strip('\"').strip(\"'\")\n    return found\n\n\ndef parse_day(raw: str) -> date | None:\n    text = (raw or \"\").strip()\n    if not text:\n        return None\n    try:\n        return date.fromisoformat(text[:10])\n    except ValueError:\n        return None\n\n\nDEAD_STATUSES = {\"superseded\", \"retired\", \"rejected\", \"deprecated\", \"archived\"}\n\n\ndef in_force(fm: dict[str, str], today: date) -> tuple[bool, str, str]:\n    valid_from = parse_day(fm.get(\"valid_from\") or fm.get(\"verified_at\") or \"\")\n    invalid_at = parse_day(fm.get(\"invalid_at\") or \"\")\n    valid_s = valid_from.isoformat() if valid_from else \"\"\n    invalid_s = invalid_at.isoformat() if invalid_at else \"\"\n    # a replaced or rejected page must not be claimed by the lock or listed in L0\n    if (fm.get(\"status\") or \"\").strip().lower() in DEAD_STATUSES:\n        return False, valid_s, invalid_s\n    if valid_from and valid_from > today:\n        return False, valid_s, invalid_s\n    if invalid_at and invalid_at <= today:\n        return False, valid_s, invalid_s\n    return True, valid_s, invalid_s\n\n\ndef live_rows(\n    rows: list[tuple[str, list[str], str, str]],\n    vault: Path | None,\n    today: date | None = None,\n) -> list[tuple[str, list[str], str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Drop expired / not-yet-valid / missing sources when a vault is given.\"\"\"\n    if vault is None:\n        return rows\n    today = today or date.today()\n    kept: list[tuple[str, list[str], str, str]] = []\n    for case_id, aliases, source, anchor in rows:\n        path = vault / source\n        if not path.is_file():\n            continue\n        live, _, _ = in_force(parse_frontmatter(path), today)\n        if live:\n            kept.append((case_id, aliases, source, anchor))\n    return kept\n\n\ndef normalize(value: str) -> str:\n    chars: list[str] = []\n    for char in value:\n        if char in PARTICLES or char.isspace():\n            continue\n        if unicodedata.category(char).startswith((\"P\", \"S\")):\n            continue\n        chars.append(char.lower())\n    return \"\".join(chars)\n\n\ndef load_rows(path: Path) -> list[tuple[str, list[str], str, str]]:\n    rows: list[tuple[str, list[str], str, str]] = []\n    for raw in path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").splitlines():\n        if not raw or raw.startswith(\"#\"):\n            continue\n        parts = raw.split(\"|\", 3)\n        if len(parts) != 4:\n            raise ValueError(f\"routing map row: {raw}\")\n        case_id, aliases_raw, source, anchor = parts\n        aliases = [item.strip() for item in aliases_raw.split(\";\") if item.strip()]\n        rows.append((case_id, aliases, source, anchor))\n    return rows\n\n\ndef stands_in_for(q: str, a: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"A query shorter than the alias may stand in for it only when it is most of it.\n\n    `how` sits inside `how to handle clippings` without meaning it, so a latin\n    fragment has to carry the alias. One CJK character already carries a word.\n    \"\"\"\n    if all(ord(char) < 128 for char in q):\n        return len(q) >= 4 and len(q) * 2 >= len(a)\n    return len(q) >= 2\n\n\nLOCK_BAND = 100\n\n\ndef carries(a: str, q: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"An alias inside a longer question locks only when it carries the question.\n\n    `日更` sits inside `日更能不能交给云端跑` without being what the question is about.\n    \"\"\"\n    return len(a) >= 4 or len(a) * 2 >= len(q)\n\n\ndef alias_score(query: str, alias: str) -> int:\n    q = normalize(query)\n    a = normalize(alias)\n    if not q or not a:\n        return 0\n    if a == q:\n        return 1000 + len(a)\n    if a in q:\n        # below LOCK_BAND: still ranks the suggestion, never claims the page\n        return 500 + len(a) if carries(a, q) else 60 + len(a)\n    if q in a and stands_in_for(q, a):\n        return 100 + len(q)\n    return 0\n\n\nHINT_FUNCTION = set(\"的了我你他她它吗呢吧啊么什怎样哪是有在要不能会该这那个\")\n\n\ndef is_cjk(char: str) -> bool:\n    return \"\\u3400\" <= char <= \"\\u9fff\"\n\n\ndef near_score(query: str, alias: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Weaker overlap for suggestions only. Never used as a canonical hit.\"\"\"\n    hit = alias_score(query, alias)\n    if hit:\n        return hit\n    q = normalize(query)\n    a = normalize(alias)\n    if len(q) < 2 or len(a) < 2:\n        return 0\n    n = 0\n    for left, right in zip(q, a):\n        if left != right:\n            break\n        n += 1\n    if n >= 2:\n        return 40 + n\n    # 汉字只算连着的双字，而且不算虚字双字：零散的单字（「剪辑」和「剪藏原件」共有「剪」「件」）、\n    # 「什么」这种问句词，都不说明问的是这一页\n    shared = {q[i:i + 2] for i in range(len(q) - 1)} & {a[i:i + 2] for i in range(len(a) - 1)}\n    shared = {b for b in shared if is_cjk(b[0]) and is_cjk(b[1]) and not set(b) & HINT_FUNCTION}\n    if shared:\n        return 21 + len(shared)\n    overlap = len({c for c in set(q) & set(a) if not is_cjk(c)})\n    if overlap >= 2:\n        return 20 + overlap\n    return 0\n\n\ndef scores_for(query: str, rows: list[tuple[str, list[str], str, str]]) -> dict[str, int]:\n    scores: dict[str, int] = {}\n    for case_id, aliases, _source, _anchor in rows:\n        best = 0\n        for alias in aliases:\n            best = max(best, alias_score(query, alias))\n        if best >= LOCK_BAND:\n            scores[case_id] = best\n    return scores\n\n\ndef pick(scores: dict[str, int], source_by_id: dict[str, str]) -> str | None:\n    if not scores:\n        return None\n    top = max(scores.values())\n    winners = [case_id for case_id, score in scores.items() if score == top]\n    if len(winners) == 1:\n        return winners[0]\n    if len({source_by_id[case_id] for case_id in winners}) == 1:\n        return sorted(winners)[0]\n    return None\n\n\ndef lookup(\n    query: str,\n    rows: list[tuple[str, list[str], str, str]],\n    vault: Path | None = None,\n    today: date | None = None,\n) -> tuple[str, str, str] | None:\n    rows = live_rows(rows, vault, today)\n    source_by_id = {case_id: source for case_id, _aliases, source, _anchor in rows}\n    winner = pick(scores_for(query, rows), source_by_id)\n    if winner is None and len(query.split()) > 1:\n        # Token fallback: only whole-alias hits count. A token that is just a fragment of an\n        # alias (`纠错` in `纠错优先级`) must not speak for the rest of `Claude Code 纠错`.\n        token_scores: dict[str, int] = {}\n        for token in query.split():\n            for case_id, score in scores_for(token, rows).items():\n                if score < 500:\n                    continue\n                token_scores[case_id] = token_scores.get(case_id, 0) + score\n        winner = pick(token_scores, source_by_id)\n    if winner is None:\n        return None\n    for case_id, _aliases, source, anchor in rows:\n        if case_id == winner:\n            return case_id, source, anchor\n    return None\n\n\ndef suggestions(\n    query: str,\n    rows: list[tuple[str, list[str], str, str]],\n    limit: int = 5,\n    vault: Path | None = None,\n    today: date | None = None,\n) -> list[tuple[int, str, str, str]]:\n    rows = live_rows(rows, vault, today)\n    ranked: list[tuple[int, str, str, str]] = []\n    for case_id, aliases, source, _anchor in rows:\n        best = 0\n        best_alias = aliases[0] if aliases else \"\"\n        for alias in aliases:\n            score = near_score(query, alias)\n            if score > best:\n                best = score\n                best_alias = alias\n        if best:\n            ranked.append((best, case_id, best_alias, source))\n    ranked.sort(key=lambda item: (-item[0], item[1]))\n    return ranked[:limit]\n\n\ndef query_conflict(\n    query: str,\n    rows: list[tuple[str, list[str], str, str]],\n    vault: Path | None = None,\n    today: date | None = None,\n) -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"Ask the host when a miss is a tie between two different pages in the hit band.\n\n    Hit band is alias_score >= 100. Weak overlap hints (20–40) are not a choice.\n    \"\"\"\n    live = live_rows(rows, vault, today)\n    if lookup(query, rows, vault=vault, today=today) is not None:\n        return None\n    source_by_id = {case_id: source for case_id, _aliases, source, _anchor in live}\n    scores = scores_for(query, live)\n    if not scores:\n        token_scores: dict[str, int] = {}\n        for token in query.split():\n            for case_id, score in scores_for(token, live).items():\n                token_scores[case_id] = token_scores.get(case_id, 0) + score\n        scores = token_scores\n    if not scores:\n        return None\n    top = max(scores.values())\n    if top < 100:\n        return None\n    winners = [case_id for case_id, score in scores.items() if score == top]\n    files = {source_by_id[cid] for cid in winners if cid in source_by_id}\n    if len(winners) < 2 or len(files) < 2:\n        return None\n    left_id, right_id = sorted(winners)[:2]\n\n    def named(case_id: str) -> tuple[str, str]:\n        for cid, aliases, source, _anchor in live:\n            if cid != case_id:\n                continue\n            best = 0\n            name = aliases[0] if aliases else case_id\n            for alias in aliases:\n                score = alias_score(query, alias)\n                if score > best:\n                    best = score\n                    name = alias\n            return name, source\n        return case_id, \"\"\n\n    left_alias, left_source = named(left_id)\n    right_alias, right_source = named(right_id)\n    return {\n        \"kind\": \"ambiguous-query\",\n        \"left\": (left_id, left_alias, left_source, top),\n        \"right\": (right_id, right_alias, right_source, top),\n        \"host_prompt\": (\n            f\"「{query}」同时打到 {left_id}（{left_alias} → {left_source}）\"\n            f\"和 {right_id}（{right_alias} → {right_source}）。锁不能猜。选一个，或说都不是。\"\n        ),\n    }\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    parser.add_argument(\"--map\", required=True)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--vault\", required=True)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--query\", default=\"\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--suggest\", action=\"store_true\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--explain\", action=\"store_true\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--limit\", type=int, default=5)\n    args = parser.parse_args()\n    rows = load_rows(Path(args.map))\n    vault = Path(args.vault)\n\n    if args.explain:\n        if not args.query:\n            return 2\n        conflict = query_conflict(args.query, rows, vault=vault)\n        if not conflict:\n            sys.stdout.write(\"conflict: no\\n\")\n            return 0\n        left_id, left_alias, left_source, left_score = conflict[\"left\"]\n        right_id, right_alias, right_source, right_score = conflict[\"right\"]\n        sys.stdout.write(\"conflict: yes\\n\")\n        sys.stdout.write(f\"conflict_kind: {conflict['kind']}\\n\")\n        sys.stdout.write(\n            f\"conflict_left: {left_id}|{left_alias}|{left_source}|{left_score}\\n\"\n        )\n        sys.stdout.write(\n            f\"conflict_right: {right_id}|{right_alias}|{right_source}|{right_score}\\n\"\n        )\n        sys.stdout.write(f\"host_prompt: {conflict['host_prompt']}\\n\")\n        return 0\n\n    if Measured, and what is not.** One-line installs get\n> the latest release; anything under \"Unreleased\" in CHANGELOG.md is on `main` only. Every fact an evaluating agent\n> needs, with sources: [`docs/FOR-AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/398894496-arch/KRouter/blob/main/docs/FOR-AGENTS.md).\n> - **Held-out bench** (200 questions on a synthetic 110-page vault, never tuned on; *not* real traffic): KRouter 26%\n>   wrong citations, 47 of 80 unanswerable questions refused, 102 of 120 answerable right. At their defaults claude-mem\n>   64% and basic-memory 78%, 72 and 45 right; neither can refuse. BM25 given KRouter's two rules (skip replaced\n>   pages, refuse a weak match) is level with KRouter: the lead is those rules being on by default, not the ranker.\n> - **Real-traffic blind test on fresh queries** ([VERIFY.md](https://github.com/398894496-arch/KRouter/blob/main/docs/VERIFY.md)\n>   layer 4): not run yet; it waits for 50 new queries.\n> - **Who wrote the held-out questions:** Claude Opus in separate claude.ai sessions, not a person. A person-written\n>   set is planned.\n> - **Releases:** 1.2.0 (2026-10-19) came ahead of the planned 2026-11-12, at the maintainer's call. From here, minor\n>   releases at most once a week and patches when ready; `KROUTER_TAG` pins one.\n> - **Nightly job:** the one-line install is lookup only and asks nothing; `--ask` asks about importing sessions and\n>   the nightly job. The manual `install.sh` installs the job (`KROUTER_NO_TIMER=1` skips). Queries never leave the machine.\n> - **Nightly writer lanes:** an API key runs nothing locally; grok (kernel sandbox) and claude (tool allow-list) are\n>   limited to the vault; Codex can read the whole account and writes only the vault, so it is used only when you name\n>   it or set `KROUTER_ALLOW_CODEX=1`; other CLIs are unconfined and are never picked unless you set\n>   `KROUTER_ALLOW_UNCONFINED=1`.\n>   [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/398894496-arch/KRouter/blob/main/SECURITY.md) has the table.\n<!-- krouter-status:end -->\n\nDoes an agent memory cite the right page, follow a correction, and refuse what it does not hold? Retrieval benches\nusually score how often the right page shows up. This one scores the opposite failure, the one users actually get\nburned by: a confident answer from the wrong page.\n\nEverything is in [`bench/memory_honesty/`](../bench/memory_honesty/): a 30-page vault of plain Markdown, 30\nquestions, a runner, and a scorer that grades any system's output.\n\n## The questions\n\n| Kind | n | What the vault holds | Right behaviour |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `correction` | 10 | an old page (`status: superseded`) and the newer page that replaces it, which also says so in its text | cite the new page first |\n| `current` | 10 | one page that answers it | cite that page first |\n| `refuse` | 10 | nothing that answers it, but a page that answers a *neighbouring* question: the search API timeout when the vault has the payments API timeout; file storage backups when it has database backups | refuse; citing the neighbour is a wrong citation |\n\n## Metrics\n\n- **Wrong-citation rate**: of the questions a system answered, the share whose first citation is not the gold page.\n  Every answered `refuse` question counts as wrong.\n- **Refusal**: `refuse` questions refused, of 10.\n- **Correction hit**: `correction` questions whose first citation is the new page, of 10.\n- **Current hit**: `current` questions whose first citation is the gold page, of 10.\n\n## Results\n\nFour systems, both question sets, run on 2026-10-12. Held-out means the 25 questions in `heldout.jsonl` that KRouter was\nnever tuned on ([`HELDOUT.md`](../bench/memory_honesty/HELDOUT.md)); dev means the 30 bench questions, on which KRouter\nwas fixed once (see below). Each cell gives the wrong-citation rate, refusals out of 10 neighbour questions, and right\nanswers on correction and current questions.\n\n| System | Held-out: wrong citations | refused | corrections | current | Dev: wrong citations | refused | corrections | current |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Plain full-text search (SQLite FTS5 BM25), always answers | 61% (14 / 23) | 1 / 10 | 4 / 9 | 5 / 6 | 63% (19 / 30) | 0 / 10 | 1 / 10 | 10 / 10 |\n| basic-memory 0.22.1, default search (vector) | 60% (15 / 25) | 0 / 10 | 4 / 9 | 6 / 6 | 39% (11 / 28) | 2 / 10 | 7 / 10 | 10 / 10 |\n| claude-mem 13.35.0, its search over what it observed | 60% (15 / 25) | 0 / 10 | 5 / 9 | 5 / 6 | 43% (13 / 30) | 0 / 10 | 7 / 10 | 10 / 10 |\n| **KRouter 1.0.1** | **25% (3 / 12)** | **8 / 10** | 5 / 9 | 4 / 6 | 0% (0 / 17) | 10 / 10 | 8 / 10 | 9 / 10 |\n\nThat table compares systems at their defaults, and at their defaults the other three have no way to refuse and no\nnotion of a replaced page, so \"neighbours refused 0 / 10\" is settled before the first question. An outside review\n(2026-10-12) pointed this out. The fair question is what an ordinary search does once it gets the same two things\nKRouter has: replaced pages left out (`status: superseded`), and a score floor below which it refuses.\n\n### Matched baselines: the same two things, for everyone\n\nEach system that reports a score gets superseded pages removed from its results and a floor picked **on the dev set\nonly**, by one fixed rule (most right answers minus wrong citations; on a tie, the lower floor), then applied\nunchanged to held-out. `run.py --adapter bm25-floor` is the BM25 version; `floor.py` does it for any scored adapter\noutput. claude-mem's search returns no score, so it has no row here.\n\n| Held-out, 25 questions | Wrong citations | Neighbours refused | Answerable right (of 15) |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| BM25 + skip superseded + dev floor | 19% (3 / 16) | 7 / 10 | 13 |\n| basic-memory 0.22.1 + skip superseded + dev floor | 30% (6 / 20) | 4 / 10 | 14 |\n| KRouter 1.0.1 (as shipped) | 25% (3 / 12) | 8 / 10 | 9 |\n\nSystems that answer more questions also cite more wrong pages, so the fair comparison is at the **same coverage**:\neach baseline's floor set so that it answers as many questions as KRouter does (12 on held-out, 17 on dev). Choosing\nan operating point on held-out is done here for baselines only, never for KRouter.\n\n| Same coverage | Held-out: wrong / right | Dev: wrong / right |\n|---|---|---|\n| BM25 + skip superseded | 2 / 10 | 1 / 16 |\n| basic-memory + skip superseded | 2 / 10 | 1 / 16 |\n| KRouter 1.0.1 | 3 / 9 | 0 / 17 (tuned on dev) |\n\n**What this says.** On this bench, KRouter's retrieval is not better than plain full-text search or basic-memory's\nembedding search once they are given the same two rules; at the same coverage it is slightly worse on held-out. Almost\nall of the gap in the first table, 61% → 25% wrong citations, comes from those two rules: a replaced page that is\nmarked and left out, and an answer withheld when the match is weak. KRouter's real difference is that it does both\nby default and says so with a receipt, in plain Markdown that several agents share. That is a design choice\nanyone can copy, not a better ranker. The bench is small (30 pages, English, 55 questions): a fair reading is \"no\nmeasurable ranking advantage\", not \"worse\".\n\nWhat the default-settings table still shows, because it is how people run these tools:\n- **Neighbour questions are where the defaults differ.** basic-memory, claude-mem and plain search answer nearly every\n  question that sounds like something in the vault, so a question about the search API timeout gets the payments API\n  timeout page. KRouter refuses 8 of 10 on held-out.\n- **KRouter pays for that in answerable questions:** 9 of 15 on held-out against 10 for basic-memory and claude-mem.\n  Five of its six misses there are refusals of a question phrased in words the page does not use.\n- **Corrections are hard at defaults.** All four put the replaced page first on some correction questions; with\n  replaced pages left out, BM25 and basic-memory get 8 and 9 of 9.\n\n### Tried and not shipped (2026-10-12)\n\nAfter the matched baselines showed no ranking advantage, a round of changes aimed at beating BM25: English stemming\n(`locally` = `local`), following `superseded_by` from a replaced page to its replacement, refusing on unknown words\nonly when they outnumber the matched ones, refusing when the question names another page's topic that the top page\nnever mentions, and answer cards that work on English pages (they had been written in Chinese and filtered out). On\nthe two dev sets (the bench's 30 and 50 more written by the maintainer, `questions_dev2.jsonl`) the change matched\nBM25+rules on coverage and beat it on refusals and wrong citations. **On held-out it was worse than what is\nshipped:** 38% wrong citations (31% with cards) against 1.0.3's 25%, and 5 of 10 neighbour questions refused instead\nof 8. The maintainer's own neighbour questions were easier than an independent writer's. It is not shipped, and the\nheld-out set was used once for this go / no-go (see `HELDOUT.md`). Generated questions also hurt BM25 on held-out\n(19% → 29%): expanding pages with paraphrases lets neighbour questions match too.\n\nHow each system was run (adapters in [`bench/memory_honesty/adapters/`](../bench/memory_honesty/adapters/), each\nsystem's defaults, isolated HOME):\n- **basic-memory 0.22.1** indexes the vault folder as a project (`basic-memory reindex`, 30 notes embedded) and\n  answers with `basic-memory tool search-notes`. Its `--hybrid` and `--vector` modes gave identical results to the\n  default. It refuses only when the search returns nothing.\n- **claude-mem 13.35.0** (Claude Code plugin from its marketplace, observer `claude-haiku-4-5`) does not index a\n  folder; it remembers sessions. It learned the vault the way it learns a user's docs: one Claude Code session read\n  all 30 pages, one Read per page, and claude-mem recorded 30 observations (10 decision, 8 change, 12 discovery). Each\n  question goes to its own search (`/api/search`, what its MCP search tool calls); results map to pages through each\n  observation's `files_read`. It has no refusal: it always returned something. Running it isolated takes one extra\n  setting: even with its own HOME, claude-mem looks for Claude Code's login in the macOS keychain, which is shared\n  across HOMEs; `CLAUDE_MEM_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set to a fresh folder keeps it off your real login, and the worker then\n  needs `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in its own environment.\n- **KRouter** runs in-process (`run.py`); BM25 is `run.py --adapter bm25`, and `--adapter bm25-floor` is BM25 with\n  superseded pages removed before indexing and the dev-picked floor.\n- **basic-memory was re-run in a Linux container** (`bench/memory_honesty/adapters/Dockerfile`) for the matched\n  baseline, recording its scores; its answers were identical to the first run on the host.\n\nRaw per-question output on the dev set, for every system, is in\n[`bench/memory_honesty/results/2026-10-12/`](../bench/memory_honesty/results/2026-10-12/); grade any of them with\n`run.py --answers`. Per-question held-out output is not published, to keep the held-out set usable (HELDOUT.md rule 3);\nonly the aggregates above are.\n\nNot run: Obsidian Smart Connections (it runs inside the Obsidian app, with no headless search to call) and Mem0 (it\nneeds an LLM and a vector store configured, and has no default to compare against). Adapters are welcome.\n\n### History on the dev set\n\n| System | Wrong-citation rate | Refused | Correction hit | Current hit |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| KRouter 0.12.1 (first run, before any change) | 22% (4 / 18) | 7 / 10 | 5 / 10 | 9 / 10 |\n| KRouter 0.13.0 to 1.0.1 | 0% (0 / 17) | 10 / 10 | 8 / 10 | 9 / 10 |\n\n**Who the \"outside reviewer\" is.** Every held-out set here, and the outside reviews in `CHANGELOG.md`, come from\nClaude Opus in claude.ai chat sessions that the maintainer starts and relays: not a human, and not the Claude Code\nsessions that change KRouter, but the same model family. \"Outside\" means a separate session that did not write the\ncode it reviews; it does not mean independent of Anthropic's models, so question wording may share that family's\nhabits. A set written by a person is planned and will be logged here before it is run.\n\n**Held-out, on questions KRouter was never tuned on.** An outside reviewer wrote 25 new questions for the same 30-page vault: 15 answerable ones phrased differently, and 10 neighbour questions. They were written independently of any tuning. KRouter 1.0: 25% wrong citations (3 / 12), 8 / 10 neighbours refused, 9 / 15 answerable right. Plain BM25 that always answers: 61%, 1 / 10. The questions are in [`bench/memory_honesty/heldout.jsonl`](../bench/memory_honesty/heldout.jsonl), frozen at 1.0.1; the rules for using them (aggregates only, no tuning toward them, what burns the set) and a log of who has seen what are in [`bench/memory_honesty/HELDOUT.md`](../bench/memory_honesty/HELDOUT.md). CI pins the questions and the vault and checks only a sanity guard against plain full-text search, never a floor. Quote this figure, or the 0.12.1 row (22%), as KRouter's wrong-citation rate, not the 0% above. The three wrong citations: a git branch-name format question cited the date-format page (both say \"format\"); a release-tag naming question and a checkout-page load-budget question each cited a neighbouring page.\n\n**Read the 0.13.0 row as a development-set number.** The bench was written for 0.13.0, and its first run found a bug:\nEnglish function words (`what`, `which`, `does`, `should`) were counted as words \"the vault has never seen\", so a\nplain English question about a page that was there got refused, while a neighbour question that happened to share\n`what` and `do` with a page got answered. 0.13.0 drops those words from ranking and refusal and lets `services` match\n`service`. The fix is general, not shaped to these 30 questions: on the author's Chinese vault the recall eval is\nidentical before and after. Still, KRouter was changed after seeing the bench, so the honest held-out figure is the\n0.12.1 row.\n\nThe 0.13.0 misses are all refusals, never wrong answers. Each one asks with a word the page does not use: a pull\nrequest \"needs approvals\" where the page says \"merge\"; an on-call \"shift\" where the page says \"rotates\"; \"locally\"\nwhere the page says \"local development\". Lexical recall cannot bridge those. An embedding system would answer them,\nand it would answer the neighbour questions too.\n\n## Second bench: a bilingual vault nobody has tuned on (2026-10-12)\n\nThe first vault now carries 105 questions on 30 pages, and a round of changes that helped both of its dev sets made\nits held-out set worse (\"Tried and not shipped\" above). So the outside reviewer wrote a second one: `vault2/`, 60\npages (30 English, 30 Chinese; 20 replaced decisions with their old pages, 20 that were not replaced), with 100\nquestions split 50 / 50 by a fixed seed into `questions_dev3.jsonl` (tune on it) and `heldout2.jsonl.gz` (never; stored\ngzipped so it does not turn up in a grep). Each set: 15 corrections, 15 current, 20 neighbour questions, half of each\nin Chinese. Every neighbour question names a term no page contains, checked in CI, so it cannot be answered by\naccident. Provenance, rules and log: [`HELDOUT.md`](../bench/memory_honesty/HELDOUT.md), \"Held-out set 2\".\n\nOn vault2 the BM25 baselines split Chinese into character pairs (otherwise every Chinese question would be \"refused\"\nfor having no Latin words, which flatters the baseline), and `bm25-floor` picks its floor on dev3.\n\n| System | heldout2: wrong citations | neighbours refused | answerable right | dev3: wrong citations | refused | answerable right |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Plain BM25, always answers | 61% (30 / 49) | 1 / 20 | 19 / 30 | 55% (27 / 49) | 1 / 20 | 22 / 30 |\n| BM25 + skip superseded + dev3-picked floor | 23% (5 / 22) | 15 / 20 | 17 / 30 | 4% (1 / 22) | 19 / 20 | 21 / 30 |\n| KRouter 1.0.3 | 33% (12 / 36) | 9 / 20 | 24 / 30 | 24% (8 / 34) | 13 / 20 | 26 / 30 |\n\nRead plainly: on questions written by someone else, on a vault nobody tuned for, KRouter answers more questions right\nthan the careful BM25 baseline (24 vs 17 of 30) but cites a wrong page more often (33% vs 23%) and refuses fewer\nneighbour questions (9 vs 15 of 20). It sits at a different point on the same trade-off, not above it. basic-memory and\nclaude-mem have not been run on vault2 yet; their adapters take the vault1 sets only.\n\n### Dense prototype on vault2 (2026-10-12, bench only, not in the product)\n\n`bench/memory_honesty/dense.py` adds a local embedding model (`paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2` through\nfastembed; questions never leave the machine) and combines it with lexical search. Tuned on dev3 only; the candidate\nwas fixed on dev3 before one heldout2 run: **`agree`**, which answers only when BM25 (Chinese by character pairs) and\nthe dense model put the same page first, both with superseded pages left out and each above a floor picked on dev3.\n\n| heldout2, 50 questions | Wrong citations | Neighbours refused | Answerable right |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| KRouter 1.0.3 (shipped) | 33% (12 / 36) | 9 / 20 | 24 / 30 |\n| BM25 + skip superseded + dev3 floor | 19% (4 / 21) | 16 / 20 | 17 / 30 |\n| **`agree`: BM25 and dense must agree** | **18% (5 / 28)** | **15 / 20** | **23 / 30** |\n| dense + skip superseded + dev3 floor | 23% (7 / 30) | 13 / 20 | 23 / 30 |\n\nRead plainly: on questions written by someone else, on a vault nobody tuned for, the agreement of two different\nretrievers keeps the careful baseline's precision and refusals while answering six more questions, and against what\nKRouter ships it cites fewer than half as many wrong pages for one fewer right answer. It is a prototype on a 60-page\nbench, not yet a feature: it needs an embedding model on the user's machine and floors that do not depend on a dev\nset of their own vault.\n\n## Third bench: 200 held-out questions on a vault nobody tunes on (2026-10-13)\n\nFifty questions cannot separate two systems: a 5 / 28 against a 5 / 22 wrong-citation rate is noise. `vault3/` has\n110 pages (English and Chinese rule pages, their replaced versions, and 20 daily logs as distractors) and 200\nheld-out questions, 80 of them neighbours, with **no dev set**: it stands for a vault KRouter has never seen. `run.py`\nnow gives 95% bootstrap intervals (`--ci`), paired intervals against another system (`--vs`), a comparison at equal\ncoverage (`--vs-matched`) and the coverage curve (`--curve`). Baseline at freeze, KRouter 1.0.3 minus BM25 with the two\nrules at KRouter's coverage: wrong-citation rate −4.3 points [−10.2, +1.4], answerable right +6 [−2, +14]. Ahead\non every point estimate, significant on none. The rule for claiming \"surpasses BM25\", and for shipping a new default,\nwas written down before any candidate ran: [`HELDOUT.md`](../bench/memory_honesty/HELDOUT.md), \"Held-out set 3\".\n\n**Other memory systems on the same 200 questions (2026-10-14).** basic-memory 0.23.2 and claude-mem 13.39.0, the\nlatest releases, at their defaults (basic-memory 0.23: full text plus semantic search, in a container; claude-mem:\nfour Claude Code sessions read every page, its haiku observer took notes, in an isolated home), registered in\nHELDOUT.md before each run.\n95% intervals in brackets.\n\n| System | wrong citations | neighbours refused (of 80) | corrections right (of 60) | current right (of 60) |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| KRouter 1.0.3, default | 27% (37 / 139) [19, 34] | 46 | 50 | 52 |\n| claude-mem 13.39.0, default | 64% (128 / 200) [58, 71] | 0 | 34 | 38 |\n| basic-memory 0.23.2, default | 78% (155 / 200) [72, 84] | 0 | 16 | 29 |\n| basic-memory + the two rules (floor from dev3) | 19% (5 / 27) [4, 33] | 76 | 3 | 19 |\n\nKRouter minus each at their defaults, paired 95% intervals: against claude-mem, wrong-citation rate −30 to −45 points,\nanswerable right +17 to +44; against basic-memory, −43 to −59 points and +43 to +72; neighbours refused +35 to +58\nagainst both. Neither has a way to refuse, and neither knows a page was replaced. With the two rules basic-memory cites few wrong pages but answers 27\nof 200 questions: its scores do not separate right from wrong well enough for one floor to keep the right answers.\nNeither tool can refuse (an empty search is the only refusal the adapters can see), so their 0 / 80 neighbour\nrefusals are structural, and the answerable-right columns are the comparison that does not depend on refusing.\nTheir raw per-question output is stored in `bench/memory_honesty/results/2026-10-14/` and regraded in CI\n(`tests/test_memory_honesty_competitors.py`). claude-mem gives no score, so it has no floor variant. mem0 and Zep were not run: both need a hosted model to\nextract memories, and none was configured.\n\n## Learning from use (2026-10-15, dev sets)\n\nKRouter's nightly learner (`reconsolidate.py`) reads the questions the router did not answer well and, when a model\nconfirms a page answers one, adds that question to the page's recall triggers. `learn_bench.py` measures what one\nnight of that does: week-1 wordings go through the router into a private query log, the learner runs once, and week-2\nwordings are scored before and after. On the dev sets, the learner as shipped through 1.1.0 made recall **worse**:\nit picked neighbour pages that only share the subject (a question about SSH keys learned onto \"where secrets live\",\na question about screen readers onto \"Accessibility\").\n\n| One night, dev pairs | learned | of them wrong | week-2 wrong citations | neighbours refused |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| vault1, learner ≤ 1.1.0 | 5 | 2 | 2 → 5 | 33 → 30 of 35 |\n| vault1, learner with proof | 3 | 0 | 2 → 2 | 33 → 33 |\n| vault2, learner ≤ 1.1.0 | 2 | 2 | 7 → 9 | 13 → 11 of 20 |\n| vault2, learner with proof | 0 | 0 | 7 → 7 | 13 → 13 |\n\nThe fix: the learner now sees the start of each candidate page and must copy the sentence that answers the question.\nA pick is learned only if the quote is on the page, is a sentence (at least four words) and shares a content word with\nthe question. That check stops made-up, fragmentary and unrelated quotes; it does not by itself tell a neighbour page\nfrom the answer (a neighbour can hold a sentence that shares a word), which is left to the model's judgement as the\nprompt asks. Inputs pages (`03 资料与证据`, clipped and pasted text) are never candidates.\n\nRead the result for what it is: **it no longer learns wrong triggers, and it learns few** (3 on vault1, 0 on vault2).\nRight answers did not change in either version, because the dev pairs are two different questions about one page,\nnot one question asked twice. Whether learning *helps* needs one intent in two wordings, written by a person:\n`bench/memory_honesty/human_set/`.\n\n## Run it\n\n```bash\npython3 bench/memory_honesty/run.py                  # KRouter, in-process\npython3 bench/memory_honesty/run.py --adapter bm25   # the plain full-text baseline\npython3 bench/memory_honesty/run.py --answers mine.jsonl\npython3 bench/memory_honesty/run.py --set heldout     # held-out set: aggregates only (HELDOUT.md)\npython3 bench/memory_honesty/run.py --set dev3        # second vault (vault2/), dev set\npython3 bench/memory_honesty/run.py --set heldout2    # second vault, held-out: aggregates only\npython3 bench/memory_honesty/run.py --set heldout3 --vs-matched bm25-floor   # third vault, equal coverage, intervals\npython3 bench/memory_honesty/run.py --set heldout3 --curve --adapter krouter  # coverage curve\n```\n\nTo grade another system, index `bench/memory_honesty/vault/` with it, ask each question in\n`bench/memory_honesty/questions.jsonl` (`q`), and write one JSON line per question:\n\n```json\n{\"id\": \"C-release\", \"cited\": [\"Engineering/Release process.md\"], \"refused\": false}\n```\n\n`cited` is in rank order and uses vault-relative paths. A system that returns chunks maps each chunk to its file.\n`refused: true` means it said it had nothing; an empty `cited` with `refused: false` counts as a refusal too. CI runs\nthe KRouter row on every push (`tests/test_memory_honesty.py`), and its floors only go up.\n"
    }
